resources.string: Only a model for this person, trained on data no earlier than %1$s, is accepted. An import error does not affect the current forecast.
Display only: data and analytics are stored in mmol/L, so switching is instant and safe.
Starting carb estimate: %1$.3f mmol/L per gram. A gram is spread through a volume proportional to body weight, so the estimate is inverse to weight. Measurements from your own data will replace it.
“High +X” hints measure the excess relative to it
The range is the green zone: TIR, the band on the chart, and the threshold below which a hint speaks up at all.
One engine for everything: the line, What-if, the watch and the hypo alert all run on the measured curve — onset 11 · peak ~60 · tail 120, ISF from your corrections. No more diverging hands.
ISF %1$.1f %2$s · onset %3$.0f min · rate peak %4$.0f min

This is the SAME curve measured below, read with a different ruler: “rate peak” is the top of the hump, the measured “peak” is the minute the curve reaches full speed. They differ by about 15 minutes by construction, not by error.
Main curve %1$.0f min · dose-dependent tail to %2$.0f min
⏱ Shape is a population prior, NOT your data
curve built, but NOT applied to the forecast — see the artifact’s divergences
measured end %1$.0f min — shorter than the domain floor of %2$.0f min: the measurement window cannot see further

Minutes from the injection: onset · active phase from and to · full end. An empty field means we compute it ourselves. A filled one takes priority over the measured curve, and we can only report where ours came out differently.
Cleared — reverted to the measured curve
⚠ Shape rejected: onset < peak < end, each within physiological bounds
⚠ Could not build a curve from these numbers
≠ Your data says %1$s %2$.2f %3$s, you entered %4$.2f — using yours
💉 ISF measured from closed corrections · episodes %1$d
💉 ISF is the artifact’s prior — no closed corrections of your own yet
One engine for everything: the line, What-if, the watch and the hypo alert all read the same model. The backup digital twin kicks in only when the physio artifact failed to build.
Personal model unavailable. Until it is restored, the backup DiaPilot model runs.
Old manual values are kept only for an emergency rollback and take no part in normal operation.
The model looks 45 minutes ahead on every minute of data. The rule’s quality is in Analysis, the “Hypo alert” card: precision, catch rate, false alarms per day.

The sound plays on the ALARM channel — heard even when the phone is on silent (but the alarm volume must be turned up, and DiaPilot added to “Do Not Disturb” exceptions if it is on at night). At night (0-7h) a quiet vibration comes first; after 5 min with no response, the full alarm follows.

Ate dextrose — alerts stay quiet for the absorption window; if glucose is still low once it passes, the alert returns (the treatment did not help). If a hypo lasts longer than “prolonged”, the full alarm repeats every 10 min, even in gentle night mode. An in-range meter reading silences alerts. Implausibly low readings (a sensor artifact) trigger “check your glucose”, not a full alarm.
Experimental: a warning before crossing the upper bound — fewer spikes toward 300 starts with 40 minutes of lead time. At night the hypo alert is more sensitive (the lower edge of the band).
My hypo plan (agree it with your doctor)
e.g. 10 g of juice, recheck in 15 min
The alert reminds you of YOUR plan verbatim — the app does not calculate treatment. Empty means the alert just asks you to check your glucose.
DiaPilot keeps its own BLE link to the sensor
No keys yet. Turn on the switch and scan the sensor (NFC) — the scan turns on streaming to DiaPilot.
⚠ The sensor holds one BLE connection: turning this on takes the stream away from xDrip. To get xDrip back, rescan the sensor there. Decryption goes through OOP2.
Training period start: %1$s. Data before this date is kept and visible in history, but the model does not learn from it.
The date cannot be in the future
Everything recorded before %1$s will be permanently deleted. These records predate the chosen training period start, and the model no longer learns from them.
Run “Export database” first — there will be nothing to restore from.
The current database will be fully replaced by the chosen backup. The app will restart. This cannot be undone — if unsure, export the current database first.
A personal browser dashboard: glucose, trend, forecast, events — refreshed every minute; the daily database copy also goes there. The server is server/ in the repository. Empty means off.

A full copy of all data (glucose, insulin, meals, labels) — to the Downloads folder. Plus, when the switch above is on, an automatic daily copy (7 files, one per weekday, named after the app id: …-auto-backup-N) — and to the cloud folder if one is chosen (point it at a Google Drive folder — Drive itself does the syncing, data goes nowhere but your own cloud). Restoring is the way to move to a new phone.
A WatchDrip-compatible local server for Zepp OS. The change takes effect after the app restarts.
Test sent to the watch (“low” flag for 3 min) — vibration within ~1-2 min

Checks BOTH paths: the “low” flag to the watch face server (45s) and the mirrored notification (like a real alert). The watch vibrates if either the watch face’s low alarm or Zepp’s notification mirroring with vibration is on.
Dim night AOD on the watch

At night the watch face almost goes dark (dim clock + glucose, red when low), the chart and everything else hidden — AOD can stay on at night without glaring. The flag reaches the watch along with the data (~1 minute of lag).
Show glucose over the lock screen
⚠ The “Display over other apps” permission is needed.
A floating tile with glucose and the trend arrow — like xDrip’s, visible without unlocking. On MIUI also turn on “Display pop-up windows” and showing on the lock screen in DiaPilot’s permissions.

A reading below the 2.0 floor, one that surfaced from a gap, or one inside an artifact spike stops counting as a reliable anchor: the forecast loses TRUSTED status and names the reason, and the hypo alert asks for a meter check instead of alarming on a value glucose cannot take. Plausible anchors are untouched. On by default.
At night, judge by the band’s lower edge

The night hypo alert fires on the LOWER edge of the forecast, not the center line — earlier and more often. On checked history this gave many alerts without a real night low, so it is off by default. Turn it on once a real low shows up that lets you judge it fully.
Turning off any of the three changes what the model learns, and takes effect after the corpus is recomputed.
